title: DesConOps relevance to ARPL
source: LuhTech Holdings, DesConOps white paper, October 2026
scope_guard: ARPL remains focused on repeatable, validated AI-assisted workflows inside Revit. DesConOps may inform workflow logic but does not expand ARPL into a general AEC production standard.

relevant_principles.desconops: Keyed input -> published requirement -> authority gate -> provenance-bearing output
relevant_principles.arpl_use: Strengthen Revit workflow packs so each task declares intent, governing requirement, validation, approval authority and evidence of completion.

relevant_principles.desconops: A change is complete only when it passes its gate with evidence
relevant_principles.arpl_use: Treat API success as insufficient. Require read-back or other deterministic proof that the intended Revit state was actually achieved.

relevant_principles.desconops: Standardize the interface, not the tool
relevant_principles.arpl_use: Describe Revit workflow intent and expected state independently of whether execution uses C#, Dynamo, MCP, a bridge or another Revit interface.

relevant_principles.desconops: Learn from completed production and feed lessons forward
relevant_principles.arpl_use: Continue converting Revit failures, corrections and validated outcomes into curator-managed rules for future agents.

not_in_scope: DesConOps production metrics as ARPL metrics
conclusion: DesConOps is useful to ARPL mainly as a validation and interface-governance reference. Its strongest contribution is reinforcing that a Revit action is not finished when it executes, but when the intended state is verified against a requirement with evidence.
